notes: The breadboard is drawn with rows f-j in the upper half and a-e in the lower half. In the catalogue's naming, bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. So the upper holes are written as '9b.i' and the lower holes as '6t.b'.
Rail hole numbers (tp.1, tn.2, tn.10, tn.25, bp.3, bn.5 and so on) are estimates from the picture. Each rail is one strip, so the exact number does not change the circuit.
The 5V wire goes to the top '+' rail. The ground wire goes to the top '-' rail, from the second GND pin on the power header, which I called GND.2.
A black wire joins the top '-' rail to the bottom '-' rail. A red wire joins the top '+' rail to the bottom '+' rail.
The speaker is not in the catalogue, so I added 'speaker-8ohm' as a new part type. Its red lead goes to the 100 ohm resistor at column 12. Its black lead goes to the ground rail.
The 100 ohm resistor sits between column 9 (pin 8 wire) and column 12 (speaker red lead).
Each FSR has one lead in the bottom '+' rail and one lead in a column (6, 16 or 24). That column also holds the 10k resistor to the bottom '-' rail and a yellow wire to an analog pin.
Analog pin mapping: A2 goes to column 6, A1 to column 16 and A0 to column 24. I traced the yellow wires in the circuit image and checked them against the schematic.
The picture shows each FSR with three drawn legs (two lines and a green shaded area). I modelled each as the catalogue 'fsr' with two ports.
The 10k resistor value is written as 10000 (ohms), following the catalogue's 'value=220' style.
